_meta.description: Document-rules config for spa — Special Power of Attorney under Powers of Attorney Act 1882 + Indian Contract Act 1872 Chapter X. SPA is LIMITED to specific transaction (e.g., 'to execute sale deed of Property X to Y at consideration Z'). Narrower and safer than GPA. Suraj Lamp warning applies where SPA authorises sale.
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. SPA MUST identify the specific transaction with precision — no open-ended powers.

title: Special Power of Attorney (Powers of Attorney Act, 1882)

causeTitle.format:
SPECIAL POWER OF ATTORNEY

KNOW ALL MEN BY THESE PRESENTS that I, {grantor_name}, son/daughter/wife of {grantor_father_name}, aged about {grantor_age} years, resident of {grantor_address}, (PAN: {grantor_pan}, Aadhaar last 4: {grantor_aadhaar_last4})
(hereinafter referred to as the "GRANTOR" / "PRINCIPAL")

do hereby nominate, constitute and appoint:

{attorney_name}, son/daughter/wife of {attorney_father_name}, aged about {attorney_age} years, resident of {attorney_address}, (PAN: {attorney_pan}, Aadhaar last 4: {attorney_aadhaar_last4})
(hereinafter referred to as the "ATTORNEY")

as my true and lawful Attorney to act in my name and on my behalf SOLELY AND EXCLUSIVELY in respect of the SPECIFIC transaction described hereinafter.

promptInstructions: Draft a SPECIAL POWER OF ATTORNEY under the Powers-of-Attorney Act, 1882 read with Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Chapter X).

SPA is distinct from GPA: SPA confers authority for ONE specific transaction or a closely-defined set of acts; GPA confers broader general authority. SPA is SAFER because attorney's scope is narrow and ends on completion.
STRUCTURE:
Para 1: Preamble — identification.
Para 2: Recital of reason — Grantor is unable to personally attend the specific transaction because [abroad / ill / out-of-station / busy / NRI / advocate-only-presence-needed].
Para 3: Appointment of Attorney.
Para 4: SPECIFIC PURPOSE — set out in full detail. Examples:

(a) Sale: 'To execute, sign, present for registration and complete all formalities for the SALE DEED in respect of [Property — full description with Schedule], in favour of [Buyer — name + address + ID], at consideration of Rs. [amount in figures and words], on terms and conditions as negotiated by the Attorney, and to receive the consideration on my behalf and deposit the same in my bank account no. [number] at [bank].'

(b) Purchase: 'To execute, sign, present for registration and complete all formalities for purchase of [Property — full description], from [Seller — name + address], at consideration of Rs. [amount], and to pay such consideration from my bank account no. [number] OR from sources approved by me.'

(c) Court representation: 'To engage advocates, sign and file vakalatnama, pleadings, affidavits, applications in [Case No. / Title], pending before [Court / Tribunal], and represent me in all proceedings therein.'

(d) Lease: 'To negotiate, execute and present for registration a Lease Deed of [Property] in favour of [Lessee], for a term of [years], at monthly rent of Rs. [amount], and security deposit of Rs. [amount], on usual commercial terms.'

(e) Bank: 'To operate my Bank Account No. [number] at [bank, branch] solely for the purpose of [withdrawing the proceeds of Sale Deed / depositing pension / paying medical bills of specified date], and for no other purpose.'

Para 5: ANCILLARY POWERS — limited to those necessary for the specific transaction (e.g., for sale: appear before SR, sign endorsements, receive consideration, give acknowledgment receipt, hand over original title deeds to buyer, sign mutation application).

Para 6: LIMITATIONS — explicit:
   (a) Attorney has NO authority beyond the specific transaction described.
   (b) Attorney cannot transact for himself or family.
   (c) Attorney cannot waive any rights of Grantor without express written consent.
   (d) Attorney cannot vary consideration / material terms without Grantor's written approval.
   (e) Attorney cannot delegate to substitute attorney.
   (f) Attorney cannot make any WILL on Grantor's behalf.
Para 7: SURAJ LAMP DISCLAIMER (if SPA authorises sale) — same as GPA: SPA does not itself transfer title; only registered Sale Deed transfers title.
Para 8: AUTO-TERMINATION — SPA shall ipso facto terminate upon completion of the specified transaction OR on [end date], whichever is earlier. Beyond such termination, attorney has no authority.
Para 9: RATIFICATION of lawful acts within scope.
Para 10: INDEMNITY by Attorney.
Para 11: REVOCATION — Grantor reserves right to revoke at any time by written notice; on revocation attorney must immediately cease and return all documents.

Para 12: STAMP DUTY — typically lower than GPA. State Article 48 schedule:
   - Generally Rs.100 to Rs.500 for ordinary SPA;
   - HIGHER where SPA authorises sale of immovable property — some states (Delhi, Haryana per Suraj Lamp directives) levy near-conveyance duty on SPA-for-sale to a non-relative; relative-SPA attracts lower duty.
   DO NOT hardcode — flag advocate to verify.
Para 13: AUTHENTICATION — notarisation mandatory; registration recommended for sale-related SPAs (and mandatory in some states); consular attestation / apostille if executed abroad.
Para 14: WITNESSES — two adult witnesses.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

Key precedent: distinguish SPA's specificity rationale from GPA — courts construe agency narrowly per S.188 ICA (authority co-extensive with business). Suraj Lamp v. State of Haryana (2012) 1 SCC 656 applies equally — sale-SPA does not transfer title.

sections.description: Authority of agent — express / implied / scope
Compulsory registration; SPA for sale of immovable property may require registration per state notifications
Power-of-Attorney holder can present for registration
Authentication of PoA — notary / SR / consular
Power of Attorney — special / general — sliding stamp rates

filing_checklist: Stamp paper of correct denomination (state Article 48; specific to SPA type)
Grantor's ID / Address proof — PAN + Aadhaar / Passport
Attorney's ID / Address proof — PAN + Aadhaar / Passport
Two passport-size photographs of grantor + attorney
Two adult witnesses with own ID proofs
NOTARISATION standard; REGISTRATION required where SPA authorises sale of immovable property per state directives (post-Suraj Lamp)
Where executed abroad: Indian Consulate attestation OR Apostille (Hague countries); authentication under S.18 Registration Act within 3 months of arrival
Where Grantor is company: Board Resolution + MOA extract
Specific transaction documents (e.g., draft sale deed, agreement to sell, case papers) referenced and attached if circumstances permit
Where SPA includes power to sell — Suraj Lamp disclaimer (sale only by registered sale deed) prominently inserted
validation_rules: transaction_description must be at least 100 characters — enforces specificity
counterparty_name must not be empty (unless transaction is sole-grantor act like own court representation — then counterparty can be 'N/A — case-specific')
if specific_transaction_type contains 'sale' — Suraj Lamp disclaimer paragraph must be inserted
if state == 'executed_abroad' — registration_or_notarisation must be consulate or apostille
